contrasts.Two: Two links run from Obed to David, not from Rahab.
contrasts.Three: Three links run from Boaz to David; starting at Rahab adds one.
contrasts.Five: Matthew’s displayed sequence has four links; this count would insert an additional link.

contrasts.Judah's king Ahaz: Hosea 11:1 explicitly names Israel; it does not identify this son as Ahaz.
contrasts.The prophet's son Jezreel: Jezreel is a child named in Hosea 1:4; Hosea 11:1 speaks of Israel’s earlier childhood.
contrasts.The priest Joshua: Joshua is the high priest in Haggai 1:1, not the subject identified in Hosea 11:1.

contrasts.Jeremiah: Matthew 2:17–18 uses Jeremiah for the lament at Ramah, not the son called out of Egypt.
contrasts.Isaiah: The son-out-of-Egypt wording matches Hosea 11:1, which names Israel.
contrasts.Micah: Matthew 2:5–6 uses Micah’s Bethlehem ruler passage; the Egypt saying comes from Hosea.

contrasts.Zechariah son of Berechiah: The prophet is identified with Berechiah and Iddo in Zechariah 1:1; the temple-court victim is explicitly Jehoiada’s son.
contrasts.Zechariah son of Jeroboam: This king of Israel was killed by Shallum (2 Kings 15:8–10), not stoned at Joash’s command.
contrasts.Zechariah father of John: Luke 1:5–13 places this priest in the account of John’s birth; the victim in Chronicles is a different priestly son.

contrasts.Megiddo: This is the battlefield context (2 Chronicles 35:22), before the servants brought the wounded king to Jerusalem.
contrasts.Riblah: This is where Zedekiah was judged (2 Kings 25:6–7), not where Chronicles says Josiah died.
contrasts.Lachish: Amaziah fled here and was killed (2 Kings 14:19); that is a different king’s death.

contrasts.Hosea: The tabernacle and star imagery in Acts 7 corresponds to Amos 5:25–27; Hosea 11:1 instead supplies Matthew’s son-out-of-Egypt saying.
contrasts.Isaiah: Isaiah is quoted later in the same speech (Acts 7:48–50); it is not the source of the earlier Moloch passage.
contrasts.Ezekiel: The wording of the cited Moloch passage corresponds to Amos, not Ezekiel; similar idolatry themes do not establish the quotation’s source.

contrasts.Ruth: Matthew names Ruth as Obed’s mother; Joshua and Hebrews name Rahab in the spy episode.
contrasts.Tamar: Matthew 1:3 identifies Tamar with Perez and Zerah; she is not the woman named in Joshua 2.
contrasts.Bathsheba: Matthew 1:6 refers to Uriah’s wife in the line of Solomon; she is not the spy-sheltering woman in Joshua.

contrasts.Gath, Nob, Adullam, Keilah: This reverses the first two cited scenes: Nob precedes Gath in 1 Samuel 21.
contrasts.Nob, Adullam, Gath, Keilah: Adullam follows the Gath episode; 1 Samuel 22:1 says David departed from there.
contrasts.Adullam, Nob, Gath, Keilah: The Adullam scene follows both Nob and Gath, rather than beginning this sequence.

contrasts.2 Samuel: This parallel account opens with Jehovah’s anger moving David, rather than naming Satan.
contrasts.1 Kings: The specified contrast is between 1 Chronicles 21:1 and 2 Samuel 24:1.
contrasts.2 Chronicles: The passage naming Satan is in 1 Chronicles 21, not 2 Chronicles.

contrasts.Jeremiah: Jeremiah 7:11 supplies the den-of-robbers part, not the house-of-prayer clause.
contrasts.Malachi: The cited house-of-prayer clause is in Isaiah 56:7, not Malachi.
contrasts.Zechariah: The cited house-of-prayer clause is in Isaiah 56:7, not Zechariah.

contrasts.Isaiah: Isaiah 1:1 explicitly lists Hezekiah among the kings.
contrasts.Micah: Micah 1:1 explicitly lists Hezekiah among the kings.
contrasts.Hosea: Hosea 1:1 explicitly lists Hezekiah among the kings.

contrasts.Two: Two links connect David to Rehoboam, but the question starts with Jesse.
contrasts.Four: The supplied sequence has four people but three links.
contrasts.Five: Five links would require two additional steps not in the supplied chain.

contrasts.A borrowed iron axe head floating: This is the Elisha episode in 2 Kings 6:5–7.
contrasts.Naaman washing in the Jordan: Elisha sent the washing instructions in 2 Kings 5:10.
contrasts.A widow filling borrowed vessels with oi: Elisha directed the widow in 2 Kings 4:1–7.

contrasts.Nahum the Elkoshite: Nahum 1:1 names Nineveh as its subject, but 2 Kings 14:25 names Jonah son of Amittai.
contrasts.Amos of Tekoa: Amos 1:1 dates his words during Jeroboam’s reign; the Nineveh commission names Jonah.
contrasts.Hosea son of Beeri: Hosea 1:1 also includes Jeroboam’s reign; the commission in Jonah 1 is not addressed to Hosea.
